name: El Morro
scope: El Morro's tiered coastal fort, bastions, sentry boxes, lighthouse and principal ramps as a coordinated bounded site.
era: surviving exterior represented by selected dated references

stories.title: El Morro: The Fortress That Guarded Spain's Empire

review.method: Qualla first; exact original government HABS photographs with individual sole-creator records and primary government-role/public-domain evidence.
review.notes: The exact original public-domain Boucher landfront photograph, two aerials and color general view confirm the paired angular bastions, deep dry moat, six-arch bridge and central sally port, domed sentry boxes, layered coastal batteries, open central court and gray lighthouse. The existing bounded fort model preserves these identifying relationships. Court arcades, hidden casemates, roof joins and precise restoration/finish are medium-fi approximations, not a measured restoration. The 1960/1998 government originals are dated evidence; no current-condition or complete fine-detail claim. City, cemetery and esplanade remain outside scope.

candidates.caption: 330-PS-6215 (USN 709019):    Any tour of San Juan, Puerto Rico, would be incomplete without a visit to the historic El Morro fortress, which stands guard over the entrance to San Juan Bay, as it did when this harbor was a haven for the Spanish galleons sailing between Panama and Seville.  The sailors view the entrance to San Juan Harbor from the main ramparts of El Morro.  The fort was actually invaded only once.   In 1598, the Earl of Cumberland landed a large force of men below San Jan and after a costly battle took both the city and the fort.  From these walls in 1593, the Spaniards defeated Sir Francis Drake and his force of 27 ships and 2,500 men.   Left to right:  HM2 Eileen Paluzzi; HM2 Joseph D. LaFreniere; HM3 Marie A. Myers; and YN3 Harold E. Baker.   Photograph released October 26, 1953.   Master Caption:   Navy Accepts Women Volunteers for Duty on the High Seas.   For the first time in history, the U.S. Navy has accepted volunteers for duty on the high seas from women in the enlisted WAVES.  Those eligible were WAVES of the Hospital Corps to fill sixty-three billets on ships of the Military Sea Transportation Service.   (4/21/2015).

originalReview.caption: 9.  Landside viewed from the southeast with moat, sally port and bridge - Castillo de San Felipe del Morro, Northwest end of San Juan, San Juan, San Juan Municipio, PR
originalReview.notes: 1960 native landside exterior confirms battered bastion, cylindrical domed sentry box, sally-port pediment and six-arch bridge over the dry moat. Dated government photograph, no private-copy source line. Modern finishes and concealed interiors are not established.

originalReview.caption: 141. Aerial view, looking southeast to northwest generally - Castillo de San Felipe del Morro, Northwest end of San Juan, San Juan, San Juan Municipio, PR
originalReview.notes: 1998 native wide aerial confirms the bounded fort plan, layered seaward terraces, open middle court, principal ramp relationships and landfront bastions. Fort occupies only part of the native view; city, cemetery and esplanade remain outside model scope. Fine details and modern alterations are not established.

originalReview.caption: 145. Aerial view, closer view - Castillo de San Felipe del Morro, Northwest end of San Juan, San Juan, San Juan Municipio, PR
originalReview.notes: 1998 native closer aerial confirms the two angular landfront bastions, deep moat, central bridge/gate, pale lighthouse lantern and lower seaward wall hierarchy. Original negative border inspected; no copied-private-source credit. Fine court arcades and present restoration details are not resolved.

originalReview.caption: 173. General view (duplicate of HABS No. PR-48-75) - Castillo de San Felipe del Morro, Northwest end of San Juan, San Juan, San Juan Municipio, PR
originalReview.notes: 1998 native color general view confirms weathered buff fort walls, darker lower battery and pale gray lighthouse. Distant view, limited fine color/finish coverage; no repaint or claim of current restoration precision. Caption duplicate refers to another government HABS view; individual record names Boucher alone and has no private source credit.
